issue_context.title: BUG: Change in behavior of replace with integer series and float to_replace
issue_context.body:
- [x] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.
- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the latest version of pandas.
- [ ] I have confirmed this bug exists on the master branch of pandas.

---

#### Code Sample, a copy-pastable example

```python
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

pd.Series([1]).replace(np.array([1.]), [0])
```

#### Problem description

As of version 1.1.5 (and earlier), the code snippet above yielded `pd.Series([0])` (i.e. the replacement took place). As of version 1.2.0 (and later), the code snippet above yields `pd.Series([1])` (i.e. the replacement does not take place). In both versions, the replacement takes place if we pass either an integer array (`np.array([1])`) or a list (`[1.]`) to `replace` instead of a float array (`np.array([1.])`). Is this change in behavior intentional?

can confirm first bad commit: [45ac7dafe280b8d5430e86f05cd63d859fcc61a9] PERF: replace_list (#38097)

review_comments: Would it be possible to test `pd.array` too? Better safe than sorry. :)

That would fail. EA is not a documented allowed type for the `to_replace` argument of the `replace` method. to be fair, nor is numpy array or tuple. The safest way to restore the old undocumented behavior is to revert #38097, but not sure that a performance hit for users passing the correct type is the way forward.

Any container, even a list, with numpy scalars will still fail. This is a fix for a specific case for an arguably incorrect usage without a perf hit for correct usage.
Slightly easier / simpler would be to parametrize over the constructor, then can also easily add `tuple` or any others
I could maybe change this to a simple `isinstance(src_list, np.array)`
